profile_text.body:
The AI Now Institute is a nonprofit founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York, NY. Its website states that it challenges and reimagines the current trajectory for AI.

The site highlights commentary from people affiliated with the institute. Senior Research Scientist Boyan Milanov argues that AI doomerism is not based on scientific work and that calls for regulation from within the industry are attempts by AI companies to set their own standards. Aya Ibrahim warned against one-size-fits-all security steps after NVIDIA announced a new agent safety platform. Chief AI Scientist Heidy Khlaaf said that acknowledging harms would not be profitable for AI companies, and in an op-ed wrote that high-risk industries from aviation to banking face independent oversight and meaningful penalties, and that AI companies should be no exception.

The institute's record lists no tracked products and no MCP servers. It is recorded as facing law exposure in New York, with a count of 459.
